statement.text:
Geometry of Water Fountain
A hemispherical fountain sprayer of radius \(r\) is at height \(h\) above horizontal ground. Its radius is small compared with the water range, so treat it as a point source. All holes eject water at speed \(v_0\), at elevation \(0<\theta<\pi/2\) above horizontal. There are \(\rho(\theta)\) holes per unit hemisphere area. Ignore air resistance and use gravitational acceleration \(g\). Part A assumes uniform hole density. Part B seeks uniform coverage on the ground.

A.1. Projectile position
Find \(x(t)\) and \(y(t)\), with the ground at \(y=0\).
A.2. Water trajectory
Eliminate time to obtain \(y(x,\theta)\) using just one type of trigonometric function.
A.3. Trajectory envelope
Derive the minimal boundary enclosing all trajectories and sketch it over the trajectories.
A.4. Landing range
Find the positive landing range \(R(\theta)\).
A.5. Zero-height range
Show that as \(h\to0\), \(R=v_0^2\sin(2\theta)/g\).
B.1. Ground annulus
Express the elemental ground annulus area in terms of \(R,R_{\mathrm{prime}}=dR/d\theta,d\theta\), taking \(R_{\mathrm{prime}}>0\).
B.2. Hole density
Determine the angular hole density up to an overall constant for uniform ground coverage. Use \(R_{\mathrm{prime}}>0\).
B.3. Flat-source distribution
For \(h=0\) and \(0<\theta<45^\circ\), find the explicit angular dependence for uniform coverage.

children.text: Horizontal acceleration vanishes and vertical acceleration is \(-g\), hence \[x=v_0t\cos\theta,\qquad y=h+v_0t\sin\theta-\tfrac12gt^2.\]

For fixed \(x\), maximize the preceding quadratic in \(u=\tan\theta\). The maximum occurs at \(u=v_0^2/(gx)\), giving \[y_{\rm env}=h+\frac{v_0^2}{2g}-\frac{gx^2}{2v_0^2}.\] Equivalently its discriminant in \(u\) vanishes. Sketch this downward parabola tangent to every trajectory, with vertex at \(x=0,y=h+v_0^2/(2g)\).
Solve \(y(t)=0\) for the positive time, then multiply by \(v_0\cos\theta\): \[R=\frac{v_0\cos\theta}{g}\left(v_0\sin\theta+\sqrt{v_0^2\sin^2\theta+2gh}\right).\]
For \(0<\theta<\pi/2\), the square root becomes \(v_0\sin\theta\). Thus \(R=2v_0^2\sin\theta\cos\theta/g=v_0^2\sin(2\theta)/g\).
The annulus has area \(dA_W=2\pi R\,dR=2\pi RR_{\mathrm{prime}}\,d\theta\). If the angle branch decreases in range, use \(|R_{\mathrm{prime}}|\).

The hemisphere band area is \(2\pi r^2\cos\theta\,d\theta\). Equal water delivery per ground area requires \(\rho\,2\pi r^2\cos\theta\,d\theta\propto2\pi RR_{\mathrm{prime}}\,d\theta\), so \[\rho(\theta)\propto\frac{RR_{\mathrm{prime}}}{r^2\cos\theta}.\]

With \(R=v_0^2\sin2\theta/g\) and \(R_{\mathrm{prime}}=2v_0^2\cos2\theta/g\), \[\rho\propto\frac{v_0^4}{g^2r^2}\frac{\sin4\theta}{\cos\theta}.\] The requested angular shape is \(\sin4\theta/\cos\theta\). Restricting the angle avoids two launch angles delivering water to the same ring.

solution.text:
Geometry of Water Fountain
A.1. Projectile position
Horizontal acceleration vanishes and vertical acceleration is \(-g\), hence \[x=v_0t\cos\theta,\qquad y=h+v_0t\sin\theta-\tfrac12gt^2.\]
A.2. Water trajectory
Substitute \(t=x/(v_0\cos\theta)\) and \(\sec^2\theta=1+\tan^2\theta\): \[y=h+x\tan\theta-\frac{gx^2}{2v_0^2}(1+\tan^2\theta).\]
A.3. Trajectory envelope
For fixed \(x\), maximize the preceding quadratic in \(u=\tan\theta\). The maximum occurs at \(u=v_0^2/(gx)\), giving \[y_{\rm env}=h+\frac{v_0^2}{2g}-\frac{gx^2}{2v_0^2}.\] Equivalently its discriminant in \(u\) vanishes. Sketch this downward parabola tangent to every trajectory, with vertex at \(x=0,y=h+v_0^2/(2g)\).
A.4. Landing range
Solve \(y(t)=0\) for the positive time, then multiply by \(v_0\cos\theta\): \[R=\frac{v_0\cos\theta}{g}\left(v_0\sin\theta+\sqrt{v_0^2\sin^2\theta+2gh}\right).\]
A.5. Zero-height range
For \(0<\theta<\pi/2\), the square root becomes \(v_0\sin\theta\). Thus \(R=2v_0^2\sin\theta\cos\theta/g=v_0^2\sin(2\theta)/g\).
B.1. Ground annulus
The annulus has area \(dA_W=2\pi R\,dR=2\pi RR_{\mathrm{prime}}\,d\theta\). If the angle branch decreases in range, use \(|R_{\mathrm{prime}}|\).
B.2. Hole density
The hemisphere band area is \(2\pi r^2\cos\theta\,d\theta\). Equal water delivery per ground area requires \(\rho\,2\pi r^2\cos\theta\,d\theta\propto2\pi RR_{\mathrm{prime}}\,d\theta\), so \[\rho(\theta)\propto\frac{RR_{\mathrm{prime}}}{r^2\cos\theta}.\]
B.3. Flat-source distribution
With \(R=v_0^2\sin2\theta/g\) and \(R_{\mathrm{prime}}=2v_0^2\cos2\theta/g\), \[\rho\propto\frac{v_0^4}{g^2r^2}\frac{\sin4\theta}{\cos\theta}.\] The requested angular shape is \(\sin4\theta/\cos\theta\). Restricting the angle avoids two launch angles delivering water to the same ring.
